correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation of the printed reaction terms gives the stated Jacobian. At the published equilibrium the zero-mode trace is negative and determinant positive. For the Figure 3 diffusion coefficients the linear coefficient in the modal determinant has the sign that makes every coefficient positive, while the modal trace decreases with spatial eigenvalue. This proves linear stability for every mode. A standalone numerical replay independently solves the equilibrium and checks derivatives by finite differences.

value.rationale: Figure 3 is used by the source to support the claimed diffusion-driven transition from instability to stability as prey diffusion increases. Showing that the advertised unstable case is actually linearly stable for every spatial mode directly changes the interpretation of a central numerical example and separates possible finite-amplitude spatial structure from genuine Turing instability.
